baselineDisplay.title: Flying cats
baselineDisplay.text:
Step 1: Intensive reading.
Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: How do cats try to protect themselves when falling from great heights?
Answer: They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels to increase their air-resistance.
Vocabulary:
fascinate v. 迷住，吸引住
independence n. 独立，独立性
affectionate adj. 充满深情的，柔情的
high-rise adj. 高层的
windowsill n. 窗槛
mysterious adj. 神秘的，难以理解的
paratrooper n. 伞兵
squirrel n. 松鼠
submissive adj. 服从的，顺从的
air-resistance n. 空气阻力
feline adj. 猫的
impact n. 冲击力
Passage:
Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well. They never become submissive like dogs and horses. As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence. Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives. One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives. Apparently, there is a good deal of truth in this idea. A cat's ability to survive falls is based on fact.
猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。它们可以对人友好，充满柔情。但是，它们又有自己神秘的生活方式。它们从不像狗和马一样变得那么顺从。结果是人们已经学会尊重猫的独立性。在它们的一生中，大多数猫都对人存有戒心。最使我们感兴趣的一件事情就是一种通俗的信念——猫有九条命。显然，这种说法里面包含着许多真实性。猫在跌落时能够大难不死是有事实作为依据的。
Notes:
1 Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. 在这句话中有一个否定词 never 和一个含有否定意义的动词 fail，这两个否定词就组成了双重否定，而双重否定往往用来表示肯定。这句话可以译成：“猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。”
2 be based on，在……基础之上。
Recently the New York Animal Medical Centre made a study of 132 cats over a period of five months. All these cats had one experience in common: they had fallen off high buildings, yet only eight of them died from shock or injuries. Of course, New York is the ideal place for such an interesting study, because there is no shortage of tall buildings. There are plenty of high-rise windowsills to fall from! One cat, Sabrina, fell 32 storeys, yet only suffered from a broken tooth. ‘Cats behave like well-trained paratroopers,’ a doctor said. It seems that the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves. In a long drop, they reach speeds of 60 miles an hour and more. At high speeds, falling cats have time to relax. They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels. This increases their air-resistance and reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.
最近，纽约动物医疗中心对 132 只猫进行了为期 5 个月的综合研究。所有这些猫都有一个共同的经历：它们都曾从高层建筑上摔下来过，但只有其中的 8 只猫死于震荡或跌伤。当然，纽约是进行这种有趣的试验的一个理想的地方，因为那里根本不缺乏高楼大厦，有的是高层的窗槛从上往下坠落。有一只叫萨伯瑞娜的猫从 32 层楼上掉下来，但只摔断了一颗牙。“猫就像训练有素的跳伞队员，”一位医生说。看起来，猫跌落的距离越长，它们就越不会受到伤害。在一个长长的跌落过程中，它们可以达到每小时 60 英里甚至更快的速度。在高速下落中，猫有时间放松自己。它们伸展开四肢，就像飞行中的松鼠一样。这样就加大了空气阻力，并减小了它们着地时冲击力带来的震动。
Notes:
3 have in common，有共同之处。
4 the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves，猫跌落的距离越长，它们就越不会伤害自己。“the + 形容词或副词比较级 …the + 形容词或副词比较级”的结构常用来表示比较关系，往往可以译成“越……越……”。 be likely to 是“很可能会”的意思。
9.2【阅读理解】Flying cats
Step 2: Comprehension questions.
Comprehension:
1 How do cats often behave towards humans? (They can be friendly and affectionate.)
2 But they're suspicious of humans as well, aren't they? (Yes, they are.)
3 Do they lead mysterious lives of their own? (Yes, they do.)
4 How are they different from dogs and horses? (They never become submissive.)
5 What have humans learned to respect about cats? (Their independence.)
6 What is the popular belief about cats? (That they have nine lives.)
7 Is there any truth in this belief? (Yes, there is.)
8 Which institution recently made a study of cats? (The New York Animal Medical Centre.)
9 How many cats took part in this study? (132.)
10 What did all these cats have in common? (They had all fallen off high buildings.)
11 How many of them had died? (Only eight of them.)
12 Why is New York the ideal place for this kind of study? (Because there is no shortage of tall buildings.)
13 What had the cat called Sabrina suffered from? (A broken tooth.)
14 What did doctor compare falling cats with? (Well-trained paratroopers.)
15 What seems to happen to cats the further they fall? (They are less likely to injure themselves.)
16 What speeds do they reach in a long drop? (Sixty miles an hour and more.)
17 What do cats have time to do during long drop? (They have time to relax.)
18 What do they do with the legs when falling? (They stretch them out.)
19 What other animals do this? (Flying squirrels.)
20 What effect does increased air-resistance have? (It reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.)
9.3【拓展写作】Flying cats
Step 3: Composition
Write an account of cats as pets. Expand the following into a paragraph of about 150 words.
Human beings like to keep dogs and... Dogs are..., but cats like to… Cats are especially lovable when they are still kittens. As kittens they... That’s how they learn to... A lot of people keep cats so they... As kittens grow into cats, they like to … They like regular meal times and enjoy … However, they also... During the day time and at night they like to... Sometimes during the night… Cats are very clean animals. You often see them...Human beings...
Key to composition
Human beings like to keep dogs and cats. Dogs are submissive and faithful to their masters, but cats like to be independent. Cats are especially lovable when they are still kittens. As kittens they like to play by chasing anything that moves. That's how they learn to hunt mice, birds, insects and other small creatures. A lot of people keep cats so they can have a pet. As kittens grow into cats, they like to stay indoors. They like regular meals and enjoy sleeping in front of a nice fire. However, they also like going out. During the day time and at night they like to go hunting. Sometimes during the night they have fights with other cats. Cats are very clean animals. You often see them washing themselves. Human beings are fascinated by their behaviour because cats are domestic animals, while at the same time they enjoy their independence. (150 words)
课外练习：
1 We find cats endlessly fascinating because ________.
(a) we feel there is good deal we do not know about their lives
(b) we believe that cats have nine lives
(c) they are different from dogs and horses
(d) they can reach a speed of 60 miles an hour while falling
2 A recent study of 132 cats in New York proved ________.
(a) that it is true that cats have nine lives
(b) that cats are related to flying squirrels
(c) they are different from dogs and horses
(d) that cats falling from great heights are seldom killed
3 Cats can survive great falls mainly because ________.
(a) the further they fall, the less likely they are to injure themselves
(b) a cat’s ability to survive is based on fact
(c) a falling cat relaxes its legs and so increases its air-resistance
(d) they are unlikely to exceed a speed of about 60 miles an hour
4 Cats have an unfailing fascination ________ most people.
(a) with
(b) to
(c) for
(d) at
5 Cats never become submissive ________.
(a) as dogs and horses
(b) in the way that dogs and horses do
(c) as far as dogs and horses
(d) as for dogs and horses
6 ________ popularly believed that cats have nine lives.
(a) There is
(b) Is
(c) This is
(d) It is
7 New York is ideal for this study because ________ high-rise- buildings.
(a) there is plenty of
(b) of the number
(c) it has plenty
(d) the number
8 Over a period of five months, there was ________ of 132 cats in New York.
(a) a study
(b) studied
(c) some studies
(d) studying
9 Most cats are suspicious of human beings ________ their lives.
(a) during
(b) throughout
(c) through
(d) while
10 ________ there is a good deal of truth in this idea.
(a) As matter of fact
(b) In the event
(c) It would seem
(d) Surprisingly enough
11 That cats can survive falls from great heights is by the facts.
(a) explained
(b) tested
(c) supported
(d) borne
12 One cat fell 32 storeys. ________ she only suffered a broken tooth.
(a) Even so
(b) Although
(c) Moreover
(d) In spite of
答案：1 a 2 d 3 a 4 c 5 b 6 d 7 b 8 a 9 b 10 c 11 c 12 a

display.title: Flying cats
display.text:
Step 1: Intensive reading.
Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: What may spreading the legs do during a fall?
Answer: It may increase air resistance, but it does not make a fall safe.
Vocabulary:
fascinate v. 迷住，吸引住
independence n. 独立，独立性
affectionate adj. 充满深情的，柔情的
high-rise adj. 高层的
windowsill n. 窗槛
mysterious adj. 神秘的，难以理解的
paratrooper n. 伞兵
squirrel n. 松鼠
submissive adj. 服从的，顺从的
air resistance n. 空气阻力
feline adj. 猫的
impact n. 冲击力
Passage:
编者说明：原教材把病例研究概括成“跌得越高越安全”，并遗漏死亡分类和32层病例的气胸伤情。本课据1987年原论文及2025年后续研究作编辑修正。病例资料来自被送到医院的动物，不能直接代表所有坠楼的猫；文中的物理解释是研究者提出的假说，不是安全保证。
Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well. They often seem independent, though their behaviour varies. Some cats remain cautious around unfamiliar people. One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives. This is a saying, not a biological fact. Cats can sometimes survive high falls, but they can also be seriously injured or killed.
猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。它们可以对人友好、充满柔情，也有自己神秘的生活方式。它们常给人独立的印象，不过不同猫的行为有所差异。一些猫对陌生人保持警惕。最令人感兴趣的说法之一是“猫有九条命”。这是一句俗语，并非生物学事实。猫有时能从高处坠落后生还，但也可能重伤或死亡。
Notes:
1 Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. 在这句话中有一个否定词 never 和一个含有否定意义的动词 fail，这两个否定词就组成了双重否定，而双重否定往往用来表示肯定。这句话可以译成：“猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。”
2 be based on，在……基础之上。
A paper published in 1987 described 132 cats brought to the Animal Medical Center in New York during five months in 1984 after falls from buildings. Of these, 104 survived; 17 were euthanised, three arrived dead, and eight died after admission. The cat that fell 32 storeys had a chipped tooth and mild pneumothorax, not just a dental injury. The researchers proposed that cats might relax and spread their legs during a long fall, increasing air resistance. They estimated a terminal speed of about 60 miles an hour for an average-sized cat in a spread-out position. These observations do not establish that greater heights are safer. A later study, published in 2025, found more severe injuries as fall height increased. Surviving a fall is not the same as escaping injury.
1987年发表的一篇论文描述了1984年五个月内因从楼上坠落而被送到纽约动物医疗中心的132只猫。其中104只生还，17只被实施安乐死，3只送达时已经死亡，8只入院后死亡。那只从32层坠落的猫除了牙齿缺损，还患有轻度气胸，并非只有牙伤。研究者提出，猫在较长的下落中可能放松并伸展四肢，从而增加空气阻力。他们估计，一只体型一般、身体伸展的猫，其终端速度约为每小时60英里。这些观察不能证明跌得更高就更安全。2025年发表的后续研究发现，坠落高度增加时，伤情也更严重。幸存不等于没有受伤。
Notes:
3 have in common，有共同之处。
4 “the + 比较级 … the + 比较级”表示两种变化的对应关系，常译为“越……越……”，如 The higher the price, the fewer tickets I can buy. 原讲义用猫坠落高度与伤害作例子不准确，故改用此自编例句。be likely to 表示“可能会”。
9.2【阅读理解】Flying cats
Step 2: Comprehension questions.
Comprehension:
1 How do cats often behave towards humans? (They can be friendly and affectionate.)
2 Do all cats behave in the same way towards people? (No. Their behaviour varies.)
3 Do they lead mysterious lives of their own? (Yes, they do.)
4 What impression do cats often give? (They seem independent.)
5 Around whom may some cats remain cautious? (Unfamiliar people.)
6 What is the popular belief about cats? (That they have nine lives.)
7 Is the saying about nine lives a biological fact? (No.)
8 Which institution studied these cases? (The Animal Medical Center in New York.)
9 How many cats were included in the 1987 paper? (132.)
10 What did all these cats have in common? (They had all fallen off high buildings.)
11 How many of the 132 cats survived? (104.)
12 What were the three categories of deaths reported? (Seventeen euthanised, three dead on arrival and eight deaths after admission.)
13 What injuries did the cat that fell 32 storeys have? (A chipped tooth and mild pneumothorax.)
14 What explanation did the researchers propose? (Cats might relax and spread their legs during a long fall.)
15 Did the observations prove that higher falls are safer? (No.)
16 What terminal speed did the researchers estimate for an average-sized, spread-out cat? (About 60 miles an hour.)
17 What did the 2025 study find about height and injury severity? (Injuries became more severe as fall height increased.)
18 What may cats do with their legs during a fall? (Spread them out.)
19 Does surviving a fall mean escaping injury? (No.)
20 What may spreading the legs increase? (Air resistance.)
9.3【拓展写作】Flying cats
Step 3: Composition
Write an account of cats as pets. Expand the following into a paragraph of about 150 words.
Human beings like to keep dogs and... Dogs are..., but cats like to… Cats are especially lovable when they are still kittens. As kittens they... That’s how they learn to... A lot of people keep cats so they... As kittens grow into cats, they like to … They like regular meal times and enjoy … However, they also... During the day time and at night they like to... Sometimes during the night… Cats are very clean animals. You often see them...Human beings...
Key to composition
Human beings like to keep dogs and cats. Dogs and cats differ in their behaviour, and individual animals have different personalities. Cats are especially lovable when they are still kittens. As kittens they like to play by chasing anything that moves. That's how they learn to hunt mice, birds, insects and other small creatures. A lot of people keep cats so they can have a pet. As kittens grow into cats, they like to stay indoors. They like regular meals and enjoy sleeping in front of a nice fire. However, they also like going out. blocks.text: Step 1: Intensive reading.
Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: What may spreading the legs do during a fall?
Answer: It may increase air resistance, but it does not make a fall safe.
Vocabulary:
fascinate v. 迷住，吸引住
independence n. 独立，独立性
affectionate adj. 充满深情的，柔情的
high-rise adj. 高层的
windowsill n. 窗槛
mysterious adj. 神秘的，难以理解的
paratrooper n. 伞兵
squirrel n. 松鼠
submissive adj. 服从的，顺从的
air resistance n. 空气阻力
feline adj. 猫的
impact n. 冲击力

Passage:
编者说明：原教材把病例研究概括成“跌得越高越安全”，并遗漏死亡分类和32层病例的气胸伤情。本课据1987年原论文及2025年后续研究作编辑修正。病例资料来自被送到医院的动物，不能直接代表所有坠楼的猫；文中的物理解释是研究者提出的假说，不是安全保证。

Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans, but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well. They often seem independent, though their behaviour varies. Some cats remain cautious around unfamiliar people. One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives. This is a saying, not a biological fact. Cats can sometimes survive high falls, but they can also be seriously injured or killed.
猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。它们可以对人友好、充满柔情，也有自己神秘的生活方式。它们常给人独立的印象，不过不同猫的行为有所差异。一些猫对陌生人保持警惕。最令人感兴趣的说法之一是“猫有九条命”。这是一句俗语，并非生物学事实。猫有时能从高处坠落后生还，但也可能重伤或死亡。
Notes:
1 Cats never fail to fascinate human beings. 在这句话中有一个否定词 never 和一个含有否定意义的动词 fail，这两个否定词就组成了双重否定，而双重否定往往用来表示肯定。这句话可以译成：“猫总能引起人们的极大兴趣。”
2 be based on，在……基础之上。

A paper published in 1987 described 132 cats brought to the Animal Medical Center in New York during five months in 1984 after falls from buildings. Of these, 104 survived; 17 were euthanised, three arrived dead, and eight died after admission. The cat that fell 32 storeys had a chipped tooth and mild pneumothorax, not just a dental injury. The researchers proposed that cats might relax and spread their legs during a long fall, increasing air resistance. They estimated a terminal speed of about 60 miles an hour for an average-sized cat in a spread-out position. These observations do not establish that greater heights are safer. A later study, published in 2025, found more severe injuries as fall height increased. Surviving a fall is not the same as escaping injury.

1987年发表的一篇论文描述了1984年五个月内因从楼上坠落而被送到纽约动物医疗中心的132只猫。其中104只生还，17只被实施安乐死，3只送达时已经死亡，8只入院后死亡。那只从32层坠落的猫除了牙齿缺损，还患有轻度气胸，并非只有牙伤。研究者提出，猫在较长的下落中可能放松并伸展四肢，从而增加空气阻力。他们估计，一只体型一般、身体伸展的猫，其终端速度约为每小时60英里。这些观察不能证明跌得更高就更安全。2025年发表的后续研究发现，坠落高度增加时，伤情也更严重。幸存不等于没有受伤。
Notes:
3 have in common，有共同之处。
4 “the + 比较级 … the + 比较级”表示两种变化的对应关系，常译为“越……越……”，如 The higher the price, the fewer tickets I can buy. 原讲义用猫坠落高度与伤害作例子不准确，故改用此自编例句。be likely to 表示“可能会”。
9.2【阅读理解】Flying cats
Step 2: Comprehension questions.
Comprehension:

17 What did the 2025 study find about height and injury severity? (Injuries became more severe as fall height increased.)
18 What may cats do with their legs during a fall? (Spread them out.)
19 Does surviving a fall mean escaping injury? (No.)
20 What may spreading the legs increase? (Air resistance.)

Sometimes during the night… Cats are very clean animals. You often see them...Human beings...

As kittens grow into cats, they like to stay indoors. They like regular meals and enjoy sleeping in front of a nice fire. However, they also like going out. During the daytime and at night they like to go hunting. Sometimes during the night they have fights with other cats. Cats are very clean animals. You often see them washing themselves.
